How the interval and the gate work

Method, as implemented in conformal.py and the controller's confidence policy

The forecaster predicts link utilization 5 seconds ahead. Split conformal prediction turns that point forecast into an interval: on a held-out calibration capture, the absolute residuals are collected and their coverage quantile becomes the radius, so the interval is forecast ± radius. The artifact on this page stores that radius, the nominal coverage, and the empirical coverage measured back on the calibration rows — the guarantee is only claimed at the level the calibration data actually achieved.

ACI (adaptive conformal inference) then adjusts the radius online from the residual stream stored in the artifact, widening after misses and narrowing after hits, with the step size gamma recorded in the artifact. At decision time the controller writes one row of confidence.csv per path: prediction, lower, upper, width, whether the sample was in the model's training domain, and the confidence gate's verdict with its logged reason. The gate holds a reroute when the interval is too wide to distinguish the paths — a held gate is the safety mechanism working, not an error.

For the paper, this page is the reproducibility surface for the uncertainty claim: the artifact values are read from the calibration file at request time and every live aggregate is recomputed from the recorded confidence.csv files, with the source list naming each file used.
